items.title: Army to sustain offensive against separatists in South-east – GOC
items.summary: The GOC disclosed this while addressing participants of Army War College Nigeria Course 10/2026 during their Operational Theatre Visit to Headquarters 82 Division, Enugu on Monday. The post Army to sustain offensive against separatists in South-east – GOC appeared first on Premium Times Nigeria .
items.body:
Major-General Fadairo with participants of Army War College Nigeria during their visit to Headquarters 82 Division, Enugu

The General Officer Commanding (GOC) 82 Division, Nigerian Army, Oluremi Fadairo, has reaffirmed the division’s commitment to sustaining decisive military operations against separatist groups in the South-east.

Mr Fadairo, ‌‌‍‌‍⁠⁠‌‍‍‌‌‌‍‌who is a major-general and the commander of the Joint Task Force South-East, Operation UDO KA, said the division would continue to deal decisively with criminals undermining peace and security in the South-east.

The GOC disclosed this while addressing participants of Army War College Nigeria Course 10/2026 during their Operational Theatre Visit to Headquarters 82 Division, Enugu on Monday.

The visit, which forms a critical component of the course, formally commenced on 3 September and concluded on 6 September.

Mr Fadairo noted that the security situation within the division’s area of responsibility remained relatively stable and firmly under control.

According to him, this is because troops continue to degrade the operational capabilities of the Indigenous People of Biafra, Eastern Security Network and other criminal groups.

He highlighted that sustained intelligence-driven operations, aggressive patrols, and targeted clearance missions had dismantled criminal hideouts and disrupted their activities, significantly restricting their freedom of action across the region.

The GOC noted the successes recorded by troops in stabilising the South-east, while stressing that continuous operational assessment, intelligence exploitation, and adaptive security responses are essential to completely eliminate residual threats.

He charged the participants to leverage the knowledge and operational insights gained during the study tour to develop innovative and sustainable strategies for addressing contemporary security challenges confronting the nation.

Mr Fadairo further emphasised the importance of security forces remaining proactive, intelligence-led, and resolutely focused on protecting lives and property, while denying criminals any opportunity to establish operational footholds.

He disclosed that preparations are underway for intensified dry-season operations under Operation EASTERN SANITY II, with emphasis on maintaining operational pressure and preventing the resurgence of criminal networks.

“The armed forces will continue to employ lawful and decisive measures against elements whose activities threaten national security,” he said.

The GOC said the division would continue to discharge its duties in close coordination with other security agencies and relevant stakeholders.

Major highlights of the visit included tours of sectors’ areas of responsibilities, a visit to the National War Museum, wargaming exercises, and a series of presentations on the operational achievements and challenges of Joint Task Force South-East, Operation UDO KA.

These sessions provided participants with practical insights into the operational environment, lessons learned, and the complexities of countering asymmetric threats in the South-east.

They were also provided insights on ongoing peace-building processes aimed at consolidating stability in the region.

The incident was reported by Nigerians who were at the venue of the exercise, with posts shared on X alleging […] NIS passport: Venue owner allegedly denies Nig
items.body: Nigerians in Manchester, United Kingdom, were reportedly denied access to a venue where the Nigeria Immigration Service, NIS, was scheduled to attend to passport applications on Monday after the Lebanese owner alleged he had not been paid. The incident was reported by Nigerians who were at the venue of the exercise, with posts shared on X alleging that the venue owner refused to allow applicants into the centre and complained about the lack of security. The NIS had organised the exercise to attend to outstanding passport applications and renewals for Nigerians in the UK. ​ Applicants at the venue said only a few people were attended to several hours after the exercise commenced. One applicant, in a post on X, said the venue owner told those present that he had not received payment and that there was no staff or security at the centre. “He said he hasn’t been paid, no staff, no security. 3 people attended to in 1 hour,” the applicant wrote. UK police were reportedly called to the venue during the incident. The NIS has not reacted to the alleged payment dispute or the complaints over security and staffing as of the time of filing this report. items.title: Abuja Building Collapses Hours After FCTA Seal, Rescue Operation Underway
items.summary: Men of the Federal Capital Territory Fire Service are at the scene conducting rescue operations, while three ambulances have also been stationed at the location. The post Abuja Building Collapses Hours After FCTA Seal, Rescue Operation Underway appeared first on Channels Television .
items.body: A building has collapsed in Wuse Zone 4, Abuja, with rescue operations currently underway at the scene. Men of the FCT Fire Service are at the scene conducting rescue operations, while three ambulances have also been stationed at the location. The FCT Police Command said it received a distress call about the building collapse at approximately 7:45 p.m. on Monday, September 7, 2026. A police response team led by the Assistant Commissioner of Police, Department of Operations, ACP Edward Akaniyene, and the Area Commander, Metro, ACP Georgelyn Ufomadu, promptly responded to the scene. Personnel from the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA), Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), Federal Roads Maintenance Agency (FERMA), Federal Fire Service (FFS), Security Service Department, Federal Capital Territory Administration (FCTA) and other relevant emergency response agencies also joined the rescue and search operations. The FCTA Development Control Department had earlier sealed the building and directed its occupants to vacate the premises. The police said preliminary investigations revealed that the building had earlier been marked and sealed by the Department of Development Control, Abuja. So far, no victims have been confirmed, according to the police, although search and rescue operations are still ongoing to identify and rescue any persons who may be trapped in the rubble. The police said investigation was also ongoing to determine the circumstances and possible cause of the building collapse. The Command urged residents to remain calm and security-conscious, avoid the affected area and cooperate with emergency responders to facilitate the ongoing rescue operations. Members of the public were also advised to promptly report any suspicious activity or emergency to the Command through the emergency lines: 08032003913 and 08061581938. See more photos from the building collapse below: The post Abuja Building Collapses Hours After FCTA Seal, Rescue Operation Underway appeared first on Channels Television .

items.title: ‘Our people are being murdered’ – MACBAN cries out over Niger, Kebbi attacks
items.summary: The Miyetti Allah Cattle Breeders Association of Nigeria, MACBAN, has called on the Federal Government and the governments of Niger and Kebbi States to urgently intervene over alleged attacks and displacement of Fulani pastoralists in parts of the two states. In a statement signed by its National Secretary, Bello Aliyu Gotomo, the association described the […] ‘Our people are being murdered’ – MAC
items.body: The Miyetti Allah Cattle Breeders Association of Nigeria, MACBAN, has called on the Federal Government and the governments of Niger and Kebbi States to urgently intervene over alleged attacks and displacement of Fulani pastoralists in parts of the two states. In a statement signed by its National Secretary, Bello Aliyu Gotomo, the association described the situation as an emerging humanitarian crisis, alleging that attacks initially reported in Niger State had spread to the Yauri axis of Kebbi. MACBAN claimed that more than 10,000 pastoralists had fled their communities and taken refuge in Kaoje, Bagudo Local Government Area of Kebbi State. It also alleged that over 5,000 cattle were left roaming after their owners were reportedly killed or fled their communities to escape attacks. According to the association, the situation had contributed to widespread destruction of farmlands stretching from Agwara, Bargu and Kainji towards the border with the Benin Republic. MACBAN alleged that the attacks involved hunters, local tribal militias and some vigilante members, including alleged elements from neighbouring Benin Republic. The association further claimed that some cattle belonging to displaced or killed pastoralists had been stolen and transported to cattle markets in parts of southern and eastern Nigeria for sale. It said its Lagos branch was already holding some animals allegedly identified as stolen, although the claims could not be independently verified. MACBAN also alleged that stolen cattle meat was being transported from forests and illegal abattoirs into Kaduna metropolis, urging authorities to investigate the alleged cattle-rustling networks. The association called for immediate security intervention to halt the alleged killings and protect pastoralist communities in the affected areas. It also urged the authorities to identify and provide emergency assistance to displaced persons, particularly those taking refuge around Kaoje and Yauri, while conducting a comprehensive investigation into the alleged cattle-rustling networks. MACBAN said perpetrators of the attacks and cattle theft should be identified and brought to justice, irrespective of their affiliations. The association’s allegations come amid continuing security challenges and communal tensions affecting farming and pastoralist communities across parts of the North-West and North-Central regions. ‘Our people are being murdered’ – MACBAN cries out over Niger, Kebbi attacks

items.title: Foreign support for RSF major reason Sudan war persists: Sudan’s prosecutor general
items.summary: Intisar Ahmed Abdelaal calls for ‘decisive measures’ to halt external support for paramilitary group
items.body:
External support for the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) is a major reason for the prolonged war and continued violations in Sudan, the country’s prosecutor general said Monday, calling for decisive action to halt it.

Intisar Ahmed Abdelaal made the remarks during a briefing to the UN Human Rights Council’s interactive dialogue on Sudan as part of its 63rd session in Geneva, according to the Sudanese News Agency.

Abdelaal also chairs Sudan’s National Committee for Investigating Crimes and Violations of National and International Law.

“External support for the militia represents a major reason for the prolongation of the war and the continuation of violations,” she said, referring to the RSF.

She urged the council to condemn the support and take “decisive measures” to stop it.

Abdelaal renewed her call for the Human Rights Council and other UN mechanisms to support the national committee, uphold the principle of complementarity, and take immediate steps to end foreign support for the RSF.

She also reaffirmed Sudan’s rejection of external mechanisms that bypass national efforts and reiterated its opposition to the resolution establishing the Independent International Fact-Finding Mission for Sudan.

On Thursday, the UN fact-finding mission said external support networks are helping fuel the war in Sudan.

The Sudanese army and the RSF have been fighting since April 2023 in a conflict that has killed tens of thousands of people and displaced around 13 million, according to UN and international estimates.

items.title: Oseni, Olayinka and the gbewudani metaphor, By Niran Adedokun
items.summary: In the end, the issue is not whether Olayinka or anyone else finds Oseni’s choice of words offensive, but whether the political circumstances make the metaphor conceivable. And therein lies the irony. In attempting to rebuke Oseni for describing Onor as gbewudani, Olayinka offered explanations that arguably strengthened the very impression he sought to dispel. Amongst […] The post Oseni, Olayinka
items.body:
In the end, the issue is not whether Olayinka or anyone else finds Oseni’s choice of words offensive, but whether the political circumstances make the metaphor conceivable. And therein lies the irony. In attempting to rebuke Oseni for describing Onor as gbewudani , Olayinka offered explanations that arguably strengthened the very impression he sought to dispel.

Amongst many others, two things sicken me about Nigerian politicians. The first is their capacity to approbate and reprobate. You know that inclination to blow hot and cold in the same breath. The second, which flows from the first, is their compulsion to assume that Nigerians are too dumb to read between the lines. I could cite endless examples of these annoying attempts to hoodwink Nigerians in virtually every aspect of our politics, but I’ll restrain myself and focus on last week’s live-television altercation over the presidential candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP).

The facts of the “Arise Morning Show,” interview with Mr Lere Olayinka on Friday, 4 September, are in the public, so I’ll save readers the trouble of a repeat. On Friday morning, Olayinka, Senior Special Assistant to the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Mr Nyesom Wike, on Public Communication and Social Media, lashed out at Mr Rufai Oseni, one of the programme’s three anchors, and refused to answer his question.

Olayinka said in response to Oseni’s question: “Well, I’m very sorry to say this, Oseni Rufai, I don’t want to answer any question from you. I want this conversation to be among reasonable human being (sic). People who will not come and describe other people as “gbewudani…” He was thereafter interrupted by co-anchor, Ayo Mairo-Ese, who brought the interview to a justifiable abrupt end. Although the main premise of this article is the gbewudani metaphor, I hope to return to the question of Olayinka’s choice of words presently.

Let us begin by attempting to deconstruct the word. “Gbewudani” is one of those Yoruba expressions with imagery that says considerably more than any English translation can convey. The expression is derived from three words: gba (to take), ewu (clothes) and dani (to hold for a while). Literally, it evokes the image of someone holding another person’s clothes but for a moment. I understand that it is a traditional derogatory description of an excessively compliant man, especially a husband considered terribly beholden to his wife, such that the traditional hierarchy in a Yoruba household is inverted.

The word has, however, transcended its domestic origins and found its way into political discourse. In a 2020 study titled “Communicative Functions of Code-switching among Yoruba English Bilinguals on WhatsApp ,” Rotimi Gbenga Akinyede and Adedamola Adetokunbo Ogunmola provided an interesting illustration of the contemporary political usage of gbewudani.

On page 4176 of the essay published in the International Journal of Creative Research Thoughts (IJCRT), the authors reproduced a WhatsApp chat between two people discussing the politics of Ekiti State. One participant says, “Nobody will ever vote for this gbẹ̀wùdání,” which the accompanying English translation renders as, “Nobody will ever vote for this stooge.” Later in the exchange, the same participant says of the subject of discussion, “He is Mr Governor’s gbẹ̀wùdání, true-true,” translated as, “He is truly Mr Governor’s stooge.”

In that conversation, the expression was employed to describe a deputy governor perceived as irredeemably subservient to his principal. The researchers’ accompanying translation renders the word simply as “stooge.” In contemporary political vocabulary, therefore, gbewudani, conveys the idea of a lackey, puppet, or subordinate figure. It would suggest someone who, even though possessing the title and trappings of an office, is perceived to exercise less independence or authority than their position confers.

That was essentially Oseni’s description of presidential candidate, Senator Sandy Onor, in his analysis of Mr Wike’s restatement of his commitment to supporting President Bola Tinubu’s second term, even though his party, the PDP, is fielding a candidate.

Even Olayinka made an extraordinary revelation, which unwittingly lent further plausibility to the gbewudani narrative in his Friday defence of Wike. According to him, the minister had told Onor that he was free to contest the presidential election, even though the current state of the PDP would make it difficult for the party to make much impact.

In considering this fact, we must also take cognisance of the fact that this candidate will be representing what is popularly described as the “Wike-backed faction of the PDP.” In the battle of wits that hit the PDP in the past few years, Wike held the party by the jugular, coming out triumphant in the courts and on the political field at the end of the day. He spoke loudly about why he is qualified to take leadership of the PDP and has never shied away from being described as the power behind the throne. In February, two PDP candidates in the local council elections in Abuja stepped down for candidates of the All Progressives Congress (APC), on what they described as “fatherly advice” from Wike.

There is even more! Although Wike was not at the event where Onor became the PDP consensus candidate in March this year, the PDP Presidential Primary Election Committee that announced the decision was headed by former Governor Samuel Ortom, one of Wike’s closest allies. The event was also held at the party’s national secretariat under the supervision of National Chairman, Abdullahi Mohammed and National Secretary, Samuel Anyanwu, two other figures associated with Wike’s tendency in the party. Wike would therefore be unable to disassociate himself from the emergence of this presidential candidate.

And to be fair to him, he doesn’t appear to suggest that. In the interview that precipitated Oseni’s intervention and use of the contentious expression, Wike portrayed Onor’s emergence as a communal decision to which he played a part. While rejecting insinuations from the panellists that Onor might be a placeholder, Wike had said: “I have said it… and whether anybody likes it or not (note the absoluteness), yes we fielded a presidential candidate, that does not mean that we have decided to win…”

So, what is the ordinary Nigerian expected to make of that? That a party fields a presidential candidate without deciding to win? And, if that is indeed the disposition of the political establishment behind Onor, where does it leave the candidate himself? Why would a grown-up man, a professor and former senator of the Federal Republic, lend himself to a presidential contest in which some of the most influential forces behind his emergence apparently do not expect victory?

Even Olayinka made an extraordinary revelation, which unwittingly lent further plausibility to the gbewudani narrative in his Friday defence of Wike. According to him, the minister had told Onor that he was free to contest the presidential election, even though the current state of the PDP would make it difficult for the party to make much impact.

Now, let us pause there for a moment. Onor did not emerge from a faction hostile to Wike. He was the sole aspirant and consensus presidential candidate of the Wike-backed PDP faction. Yet, here is Wike’s spokesman recounting a conversation in which the minister apparently tells that presidential candidate that he is “free to contest.” Free? So, who grants the permission?

It gets even more curious when you remember that Wike repeatedly announced his support for Tinubu, the man Onor must defeat to realise his presidential ambition, long before he emerged as PDP candidate. The impression this creates is that, even if the PDP candidate was unlikely to go far in the 2027 presidential election, it remained important for the party to demonstrate that it could field one. And Onor fit the bill.

Whether Oseni’s language was appropriate for television is a different debate. Political commentary has always employed metaphor, satire and occasionally brutal language to interrogate power. The useful response to an uncomfortable description from a spokesperson should therefore not be outrage, but an understanding of the circumstances that make the description plausible, followed by a strategic effort to put things straight.

Olayinka then suggested something even more intriguing. He argued that not everyone who contests an election expects to win. Some candidates, he said, merely contest to “register their presence.”

He claimed he was speaking generally, even mentioning candidates from other parties who, in his estimation, stand no chance of winning in the 2027 presidential election. However, coming in the context of his defence of Wike’s position, the observation leaves an irresistible question: Does Wike regard the presidential candidate of his own political tendency as one of those merely regis

items.title: Police arrest four over mob killing of man on Lagos Island
items.summary: The Lagos State Police Command has arrested four suspects over the alleged mob killing of a man identified as Basit Kolade following a road traffic incident on Freeman Street, Lagos Island. The suspects were arrested after the command intensified efforts to identify individuals allegedly involved in the attack, according to a statement issued by the […] Police arrest four over mob killing of man o
items.body: The Lagos State Police Command has arrested four suspects over the alleged mob killing of a man identified as Basit Kolade following a road traffic incident on Freeman Street, Lagos Island. The suspects were arrested after the command intensified efforts to identify individuals allegedly involved in the attack, according to a statement issued by the Police Public Relations Officer, SP Abimbola Adebisi, on Monday, September 7, 2026. The police said the incident occurred at about 10:40 p.m. on Wednesday, September 2, when Kolade was travelling with his spouse from Ebute Metta towards Lagos Island in a black Lexus Jeep with registration number KSF 115 JZ. According to the command, a motorcycle allegedly collided with the vehicle from behind, leading to an argument between Kolade and the rider. The situation reportedly escalated when the vehicle reversed and struck the motorcycle, causing the rider and the motorcycle to fall. The police said the incident attracted a crowd, some of whom allegedly attacked Kolade with dangerous weapons. While some women in the area reportedly intervened to rescue his wife, Kolade was taken to the Lagos Island General Hospital, where he was pronounced dead. The motorcycle rider survived the incident and is currently receiving medical treatment at a hospital, the command said. The four suspects arrested in connection with the alleged mob attack were identified as Khalid Rafiq, 20; Gafar Rahim, 21; Ibrahim Azeez, 33; and Samos Momoh, 21. The command said investigators were making efforts to apprehend other suspects believed to have participated in the attack. The case has been treated as a homicide and transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department, SCID, Panti, for further investigation and possible prosecution. The police warned residents against mob action and other forms of jungle justice, stressing that individuals or groups have no legal authority to arrest, prosecute, convict or execute anyone. “The Command therefore warns members of the public against mob action, jungle justice, and the resort to self-help under any circumstance. No individual or group has the legal authority to arrest, try, convict, or execute another person,” the statement said. The command also cited the 1999 Constitution, which guarantees the right to life, and the Criminal Law of Lagos State, under which unlawful killing constitutes an offence. According to the police, the position is in line with a directive from the Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Rilwan Disu, that cases involving mob attacks resulting in death should be treated as homicide. The IGP, the command added, had warned that anyone who participates in, organises, incites or supports such attacks would be dealt with in accordance with the law. The police stressed that an allegation or suspicion of wrongdoing does not justify violence against any individual. “Members of the public are urged to promptly report criminal incidents to the Police and allow the law to take its course,” the statement added. The Commissioner of Police, Lagos State Command, CP Tijani Fatai, directed investigators to identify and arrest all persons found culpable in the incident and ensure they are prosecuted in accordance with the law. The command assured the public that the investigation would be conducted thoroughly and professionally, adding that anyone found to have participated in the attack or contributed to Kolade’s death would be brought to justice. Police arrest four over mob killing of man on Lagos Island

items.title: El-Rufai’s Lawyers Demand ₦10bn From Defence Minister Over Alleged Defamation
items.summary: The lawyers maintained that none of the allegations had been tested, proved or determined by a court of competent jurisdiction and demanded strict proof of the claims. The post El-Rufai’s Lawyers Demand ₦10bn From Defence Minister Over Alleged Defamation appeared first on Channels Television .
items.body: Lawyers to former Kaduna State Governor, Nasir El-Rufai, have demanded ₦10 billion in damages from the Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa (retd.), over alleged defamatory remarks concerning their client. The demand was contained in a letter before action dated September 7, 2026, and addressed to the Defence Minister at the Federal Ministry of Defence in Abuja. The legal action followed Musa’s appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today on September 3, 2026, where he spoke about insecurity in Kaduna State and made allegations concerning the former governor. According to the letter, the minister allegedly accused El-Rufai of deliberately planning the killing of people in Southern Kaduna and paying bandits. The lawyers also alleged that Musa claimed El-Rufai ordered the demolition of houses and used such actions against his opponents. El-Rufai’s legal team, Akpan Ubong Chambers, described the statements as false and defamatory, arguing that they portrayed the former governor as a criminal, murderer and sponsor of banditry. The lawyers demanded a public retraction and apology from the Defence Minister, alongside N10 billion in compensation for the alleged damage to their client’s reputation. They also denied the allegation that El-Rufai paid bandits, stating that the former governor had consistently maintained that he would neither negotiate with nor pay bandits. On the issue of demolitions, the lawyers said those carried out during El-Rufai’s tenure as governor were undertaken in accordance with the law and for public purposes. They further rejected claims that the former governor’s administration divided Kaduna State along ethnic and religious lines, saying the government implemented policies aimed at promoting unity and development across the state. The lawyers maintained that none of the allegations had been tested, proved or determined by a court of competent jurisdiction and demanded strict proof of the claims. Meanwhile, the family of the former governor has separately demanded the immediate retraction of the allegation that El-Rufai actively planned killings in Southern Kaduna. In a statement issued on Monday and signed by Honourable Mohammed Bello El-Rufai on behalf of the family, the allegation was described as grave and unsubstantiated. The family said the claim was made without any evidence being presented to support it. It said while General Musa was entitled to express his personal opinions, he should also be prepared to substantiate such a serious allegation with credible evidence. The family gave the minister seven days from the date of the statement to either provide evidence supporting the allegation or issue a full public retraction and apology through the same medium. It warned that failure to do so would leave it with no option but to pursue all appropriate legal remedies available under the law. items.body: Eleven people are said to have been killed in a Boko Haram insurgency attack in Adamawa State. The attack was launched on a community in Gombi Local Government Area, which borders Hong, the LGA that has been most affected by Boko Haram attacks in recent months. DAILY POST gathered on Monday that the 11 people in the Gombi incident were killed when the insurgents attacked Dzangola community in Gombi LGA on Sunday, September 6, 2026. Commenting on the attack on Monday evening, the Speaker of the state House of Assembly, Mathiya Wesley, said the attack had come as one too many. Wesley, who hails from Hong LGA, which has been bearing the brunt of Boko Haram attacks in Adamawa State since the insurgency began, urged the authorities to find an enduring solution to give the troubled communities respite. Speaking specifically about the experience of the people of Dzangola, the Speaker said they did not deserve the wickedness meted out to them. Speaking on behalf of the House of Assembly, the Speaker told the people, “We are with you in this troubling time.” Boko Haram attack claims 11 lives in Adamawa

items.title: FG moves to end conflicting economic projections
items.summary: The Federal Government, on Monday, moved to eliminate conflicting economic projections by Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs), setting up a high-powered inter-agency committee to harmonise the macroeconomic assumptions that underpin national budgeting and economic planning. The post FG moves to end conflicting economic projections appeared first on Vanguard News .
items.body: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Federal Government, on Monday, moved to eliminate conflicting economic projections by Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs), setting up a high-powered inter-agency committee to harmonise the macroeconomic assumptions that underpin national budgeting and economic planning. The decision was one of the major outcomes of the meeting of the Economic Management Team (EMT), chaired by the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Mr. Taiwo Oyedele, in Abuja. The committee is expected to align key economic assumptions, including crude oil price and production benchmarks, exchange rate, inflation, and non-oil revenue projections used by fiscal and monetary authorities, with a view to improving budget credibility and economic policy coordination. The move followed findings from a joint budget retreat and technical validation workshop which attributed part of the country’s budget under-performance to inconsistent macroeconomic assumptions adopted by different government institutions, according to a statement by the Ministry of Finance. The committee will also address discrepancies in the reporting of key economic indicators within government and in official communications to investors, development partners and the public. The EMT also approved measures to strengthen its governance framework by expanding its mandate to include regular reviews of macroeconomic performance, deeper fiscal-monetary policy coordination, monitoring of the Renewed Hope Agenda and periodic assessment of the Federal Government’s financing needs. As part of the reforms, the EMT will now meet monthly instead of periodically, while the Federal Ministry of Finance has been designated the coordinating custodian of Nigeria’s official economic data, with relevant agencies supplying sector-specific information for harmonised public releases. The Team expressed optimism over improving economic fundamentals, noting that Nigeria’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP) grew by 4.43 per cent year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026, the strongest quarterly growth since the third quarter of 2024. It also noted that the country’s external reserves had risen above $54 billion, the highest level in almost 18 years, while the naira has appreciated to the N1,300/$ range, its strongest level in about two years. The EMT further highlighted Nigeria’s recent return to FTSE Russell’s Frontier Market Index, effective September 21, 2026, describing the development as a major boost to investor confidence and international visibility for the nation’s capital market. According to the Team, Nigeria’s public debt remains below 40 per cent of GDP, while Moody’s recently upgraded the country’s sovereign credit outlook from stable to positive. The EMT also reviewed strategies aimed at positioning agriculture as a major driver of the Federal Government’s ambition to build a $1 trillion economy by 2030. The strategy includes reducing post-harvest losses, expanding mechanisation and agro-processing, strengthening export compliance, recapitalising the Bank of Agriculture, creating a new smallholder credit window and raising agriculture’s share of private sector credit to 10 per cent by 2030. In addition, the Team assessed Nigeria’s preparations to host the Creative Africa Nexus (CANEX) 2026 and the Intra-African Trade Fair (IATF) 2027 in Lagos, directing the Ministry of Finance to coordinate funding and customs facilitation in collaboration with the Ministry of Industry, Trade and Investment. On the decisions reached at the meeting, the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Mr. Taiwo Oyedele, was quoted as saying, “Today’s decisions tighten the link between the numbers we plan with and the actual outturns. A single, harmonised set of assumptions across the fiscal and monetary authorities means fewer surprises in the budget and more credible planning for investors and all Nigerians.” The post FG moves to end conflicting economic projections appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 2026 U-20 WWC: Falconets lose 2-0 to Spain in Group F opener
items.summary: Nigeria’s Falconets began their 2026 FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup campaign on a disappointing note after losing 2-0 to Spain in their Group F opener on Monday. The post 2026 U-20 WWC: Falconets lose 2-0 to Spain in Group F opener appeared first on Vanguard News .
items.body: Nigeria’s Falconets began their 2026 FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup campaign on a disappointing note after losing 2-0 to Spain in their Group F opener on Monday. The Nigerian side, who arrived in Poland after an extensive period of preparation, struggled to break down the former champions at the Stadion Sosnowiec. Spain made a fast start and took the lead in the 13th minute through Marisa García, putting the Falconets under early pressure. Nigeria attempted to respond but found it difficult to create clear-cut opportunities against a well-organised Spanish defence. The European side maintained its advantage into the second half as the Falconets struggled to find a way back into the contest. Spain eventually doubled their lead in the 73rd minute when Alba Cerrato found the back of the net to put the result beyond Nigeria. The defeat means the Falconets will need to quickly recover as they prepare for their second Group F fixture against China on Wednesday, September 10. Head coach Moses Aduku had earlier described the opening clash with Spain as a “Cup final” and urged his players to give everything in pursuit of victory. “We are looking forward to the match against Spain with high expectations. We are ready and set to go. Spain is a good side, no doubt, but we will approach the game like a Cup final because we want to win,” Aduku said before the match. With the opening-day defeat, Nigeria’s remaining group games against China and New Caledonia have become even more important as the Falconets seek to secure qualification for the knockout stage. Nigeria are among Africa’s most successful teams at the FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup, having finished runners-up in 2010 and 2014. Spain, meanwhile, are also one of the competition’s leading sides. They won the tournament in 2022 and finished runners-up in 2018. The Falconets will now turn their attention to Wednesday’s encounter with China, where they will be looking to claim their first points of the tournament and revive their hopes of progressing from Group F. The post 2026 U-20 WWC: Falconets lose 2-0 to Spain in Group F opener appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Six Abducted Children Die In Captivity, 17 Rescued As Police Parade Suspects In Oyo
items.summary: This followed an intelligence-led investigation into a criminal network allegedly involved in the stealing, trafficking and concealment of children across state lines. The post Six Abducted Children Die In Captivity, 17 Rescued As Police Parade Suspects In Oyo appeared first on Channels Television .
items.body: Six children abducted by a suspected child-stealing and human trafficking syndicate have been confirmed dead while in captivity, the Oyo State Police Command has disclosed. The command also announced the rescue of 17 children and the arrest of seven suspects following an intelligence-led investigation into a criminal network allegedly involved in the stealing, trafficking and concealment of children across state lines. The Oyo State Commissioner of Police, CP Abimbola Olugbenga, disclosed this at a press briefing held at the Police State Headquarters, Eleyele, Ibadan on Monday. According to him, the investigation began with a petition dated July 29, 2026, submitted by Adejoke Popoola, also known as Orente Alagbo, of Sogade Area, Ariyo, Ibadan, over allegations bordering on conspiracy, cyberbullying, threat to life and defamation of character. The petition was subsequently assigned to the Anti-Kidnapping Squad on August 3. Olugbenga said that while detectives were examining the circumstances surrounding the petition, their attention was drawn to the disappearance of a three-year-old boy, Ifakunle Ifagbenro, during an annual masquerade festival in Oyo Town on June 29. The commissioner said the child had accompanied his father to his father-in-law’s family compound for the festival, while Popoola had arrived two days earlier to participate in preparations for the event. He said Popoola offered to carry the child during the event, after which both of them disappeared from the venue. The matter was subsequently reported at the Atiba Police Divisional Headquarters, Oyo Town. According to the police chief, pictorial and video materials from the event showed Popoola carrying the missing child, while digital trails and statements obtained from persons connected to the event further established that she was with the child around the time of his disappearance. Popoola was arrested on August 4 and, according to the commissioner, admitted attending the masquerade festival and subsequently leaving with the missing child. Her statement, Olugbenga said, provided the first major breakthrough into what investigators discovered to be a wider criminal network. The suspect disclosed that she had been involved in the alleged stealing of more than 15 children, aged between two and seven years, from churches, parties and other event venues within and outside Oyo State. She also reportedly identified one Adekanbi Janet, also known as Hosanna, as her partner in the alleged criminal enterprise. Adekanbi was subsequently traced to Mowe, Ogun State, where police rescued four children aged between two and four years from custody and recovered two pregnant young women. The commissioner said Adekanbi admitted knowing Popoola for about 10 years in connection with the alleged stealing and sale of children, although she denied having custody of Ifakunle. According to him, Adekanbi further disclosed that some of the stolen children were kept in custody pending their sale, while the pregnant women were allegedly cared for until delivery. Information obtained from her subsequently led detectives to the location of Ifakunle, who was rescued around the Gbagi area of Ibadan on August 20. The investigation later extended beyond Oyo State. Olugbenga said detectives travelled to Agbor, Delta State, on September 2, where four children allegedly stolen from Oyo State were rescued from their suspected buyers. Two suspects, identified as 48-year-old Christopher Joy and 53-year-old Rosemary Jesse, were arrested and allegedly confessed to involvement in the business. The development, he said, confirmed the interstate dimension of the criminal network and showed that children were being moved outside Oyo State as part of the alleged criminal enterprise. The commissioner further disclosed that the investigation uncovered an alleged ritual dimension to the activities of the syndicate. According to him, one of the suspects confessed that whenever a child died while in their custody, the body would allegedly be sold to ritualists. The disclosure reportedly led to the arrest of Muritala Fasasi, an Alfa, and Yakubu Azeez, a herbalist, who the police said had confessed to their alleged involvement in using the bodies for ritual purposes. The development came against the backdrop of a chilling testimony attributed to one of the principal suspects, who allegedly told investigators that she had stolen 13 children before her arrest. In the testimony, the suspect, nicknamed Orente, reportedly said she would visit homes and, whenever she found nobody around, take a child. Asked how much the children were sold for, she mentioned amounts ranging from N500,000 to N600,000. She also claimed to have operated in the business since October 2024. The suspect allegedly described how children could be taken from places where traditional or spiritual activities were being held, including masquerade festivals, by gaining the confidence of parents. In one account, she reportedly said she would tell parents of children with disabilities that she could help heal them before taking the children away. The six deceased children were identified as Musharaf Lawal Tajudeen, two; Greatness Adeagbo, five; Sainat Amoo, two; Taiwo Usman, two; Daniel Solomon Olayinka, seven; and Miracle Olaniyi, four. The command said the 17 rescued children are Ifakunle Ifagbenro, three; Musibau Olasupo, five; Sulaimon Osamo, seven; Murina Fidaus, three; Aminat Yusuf, three; Taiwo Olamilekan, three; an infant male aged nine days; Rafiat Waheed Babalola, two; Quwiyat Alade, five; Rejoice Divine, three; Alhaji Divine, five; Eniolorunda, three; Victoria, three; Isoma Prince, three; Roqeeba, four; Boluwatife Odedeyi, three; and Ireoluwa Elizabeth Olapade, seven. The commissioner appealed to parents and guardians who had lost their children in recent times to visit the Police Command Headquarters, Eleyele, Ibadan, to identify the rescued children and facilitate their reunification with their families. He said the command was working with other security and government agencies to uncover the full structure of the alleged network, locate other missing children, establish the circumstances surrounding the reported deaths and ensure that anyone found culpable was brought to justice. Olugbenga urged members of the public to remain vigilant and report cases of missing children to the police without delay. He particularly cautioned parents and guardians to exercise care when dealing with individuals who present themselves as traditional or spiritual healers, especially where such persons seek to separate children from their families or take them to undisclosed locations. The commissioner also appealed to members of the public with credible information that could assist the investigation to contact the police, assuring that such information would be handled professionally and, where necessary, confidentially. He reaffirmed the command’s commitment to protecting children and other vulnerable persons, dismantling criminal networks and ensuring that justice was served in accordance with the law. The post Six Abducted Children Die In Captivity, 17 Rescued As Police Parade Suspects In Oyo appeared first on Channels Television .

items.title: Carter Efe, Speed Darlington to clash in celebrity boxing bout
items.summary: Speed Darlington will be looking to revive his fortunes when he steps into the ring against Efe. The post Carter Efe, Speed Darlington to clash in celebrity boxing bout appeared first on Premium Times Nigeria .
items.body:
Carter Efe is set to face Speed Darlington in a celebrity boxing bout

Content creator and streamer Carter Efe is set to face rapper and social media personality Speed Darlington in a celebrity boxing bout scheduled for 1 October , at the Federal Palace Hotel in Lagos.

The fight, billed as “Chaos in the Ring”, was officially announced by Balmoral Promotions on Sunday. It will be held on Nigeria’s Independence Day and streamed live on DAZN.

The promoters announced the bout on Instagram, declaring: “IT’S OFFICIAL! CARTER VS SPEED. Two African stars. One ring. No excuses. On October 1, the ring decides who stands tall. Federal Palace Hotel, Lagos. Live on @daznboxing. This isn’t just a fight. It is CHAOS!”

The contest will be the first boxing meeting between Efe and Speed Darlington, but both entertainers have previously featured in Nigeria’s growing celebrity boxing circuit.

Efe enters the bout as one of the biggest names in the current celebrity boxing scene after defeating singer Habeeb “Portable” Badmus by unanimous decision in May.

The victory came at Chaos in the Ring 4, also held at the Balmoral Hall of the Federal Palace Hotel in Victoria Island, Lagos.

Efe produced a disciplined performance across the three-round contest, using movement, uppercuts, body shots and cleaner combinations to neutralise Portable’s aggressive approach.

All three judges scored the fight in Efe’s favour, handing him a 30-27 victory on their scorecards.

Businessman Emeka “E-Money” Okonkwo subsequently fulfilled a ₦50 million pledge to Efe following his victory.

Efe’s win ended Portable’s unbeaten run in the celebrity boxing circuit, having previously defeated actor Charles Okocha and Speed Darlington.

Speed Darlington will be looking to revive his fortunes when he steps into the ring against Efe.

The rapper previously faced Portable in a celebrity boxing bout in 2025, with Portable winning by technical knockout after Darlington failed to continue into the second round.

The contest followed a public disagreement between the two entertainers. Darlington had reportedly offered Portable ₦500,000 to perform at an event, but Portable rejected the offer, leading to an increasingly heated exchange between them.

Their verbal confrontation eventually spilt into the boxing ring, where Portable dominated the opening round before Darlington was unable to continue.

Darlington later attributed his defeat to supernatural forces, claiming that “juju” or charms were involved.

Darlington’s upcoming fight against Efe also follows a challenge he issued after Efe defeated Portable.

Following Efe’s victory in May, Darlington publicly mocked Portable over the result and pointed to his own previous fight against the singer.

He subsequently called out Efe for a bout, presenting himself as a different challenge from Portable and expressing confidence that he could defeat the content creator.

That challenge has now become a reality, with Efe and Darlington set to settle their rivalry inside the ring.

The fight is the latest high-profile contest to emerge from Nigeria’s increasingly popular celebrity boxing circuit, where personal rivalries, social media exchanges and entertainment have become major parts of the promotion.

Balmoral Promotions has staged several editions of the Chaos in the Ring series, combining celebrity boxing attractions with professional bouts.

The events have also featured prominent entertainers whose existing public disputes have provided much of the drama surrounding their fights.

Portable’s rivalry with Charles Okocha, for instance, previously produced a high-profile celebrity boxing contest, followed by a controversial rematch.

The 1 October contest will take place at the Federal Palace Hotel, Balmoral Convention Centre/Hall, Victoria Island, Lagos.

However, the promoters have yet to publicly announce full details of the undercard, weight classes, number of rounds, purse arrangements or the exact start time.

PREMIUM TIMES reported in July that the celebrity boxing scene recorded another high-profile clash when Okocha defeated Portable in their rematch. The bout, held under the “Chaos in the Ring” banner, ended after Portable abandoned the ring following a chaotic opening round, resulting in Okocha being declared the winner.

The rematch came after Portable had defeated Okocha in their first encounter in December 2023. Their rivalry was reportedly fuelled by a dispute over an alleged ₦40 million business deal, adding to the personal drama that has become a defining feature of Nigeria’s celebrity boxing circuit.

items.title: Nigeria’s security agencies engaged in 7,062 operations, killed 1,487 terrorists in two months – ONSA
items.summary: The ONSA says the successful operations in July and August highlight an increasingly coordinated, intelligence-driven approach to tackling terrorism, banditry, kidnapping, arms trafficking and other emerging security threats. The post Nigeria’s security agencies engaged in 7,062 operations, killed 1,487 terrorists in two months – ONSA appeared first on Premium Times Nigeria .
items.body:
The Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA) says successful operations by Nigeria’s security agencies in July and August highlight an increasingly coordinated, intelligence-driven approach to tackling terrorism, banditry, kidnapping, arms trafficking and other emerging security threats.

This is contained in a third-quarter national security update by Chido Onumah, Special Adviser to the National Security Adviser on Strategic Communication and Civil Society Liaison, released on Monday in Abuja.

Mr Onumah said the security agencies conducted 7,062 operations, neutralising 1,487 terrorists and insurgents and rescuing 777 kidnapped victims in July and August nationwide.

According to him, the operations also led to the arrest of 354 suspects and the recovery of firearms, ammunition and Improvised Explosive Devices.

He said the results demonstrated the growing importance of intelligence sharing and operational coordination among security and law enforcement agencies.

Mr Onumah said that no single institution could secure Nigeria on its own, stressing the need for intelligence, border management, financial intelligence, emergency preparedness and community engagement.

He said the Nigeria Police Force (NPF) also recorded significant gains through intelligence-led operations, arresting 1,334 suspects and rescuing 383 kidnapped victims.

The police, he said, recovered 175 firearms and more than 3,790 rounds of ammunition while disrupting kidnapping, armed robbery, cultism and gunrunning networks.

Mr Onumah said the State Security Services complemented the efforts through intelligence-driven operations against arms trafficking, terrorism, kidnapping and other threats.

He said the agency’s interventions disrupted illicit supply chains, facilitated hostage rescues and contributed to convictions for serious security offences.

The security adviser also highlighted the growing focus on dismantling the networks that finance and sustain criminal activities.

He said the National Centre for the Control of Small Arms and Light Weapons destroyed 1,419 illicit weapons on 30 July, bringing weapons destroyed since 2022 to more than 19,000.

Mr Onumah said the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) further strengthened the effort in August by handing over 399 intercepted firearms and hundreds of firearm components to the Centre.

He said the development demonstrated how border enforcement, intelligence and arms-control institutions could operate as interconnected components of the national security architecture.

According to him, the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) conducted 2,298 targeted operations between July and August, arresting 3,705 suspects and securing 471 convictions.

“It also seized almost 54,000kg of illicit drugs and obtained court orders freezing accounts containing more than ₦9.8 billion linked to cartel operations.

Mr Onumah said the figures underscored the importance of following the money because organised crime depended on networks of financiers, facilitators, transporters and criminal entrepreneurs.

He said the Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit (NFIU) was deepening cooperation with security and law-enforcement agencies to identify financial structures supporting organised crime and terrorism.

Beyond conventional security operations, he said agencies were also addressing human trafficking, irregular migration, cyber-enabled crime and climate-related emergencies.

According to him, the Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS) rescued trafficking victims, identified persons of interest and dismantled elements of a fraudulent transnational organised crime syndicate during the period.

“Similarly, the National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons intensified operations against human trafficking and online exploitation, securing convictions and rescuing suspected victims,” he said.

Mr Onumah said flood preparedness and emergency response were also critical components of national security and resilience.

He said the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) provided relief assistance to 24,625 households, representing about 147,750 people, during the period.

According to him, the agency also activated its National Emergency Operations Centre to strengthen information management, coordination and decision-making during the flood season.

“This, too, is national security. Disasters could destroy livelihoods, displace communities and intensify competition over scarce resources,” he added

Mr Onumah said credible information was becoming a critical national security asset amid increasing misinformation, fabricated videos, manipulated images and rumours.

According to him, the Defence Headquarters (DHQ) issued 137 press releases and identified and countered 13 instances of misinformation during July and August.

He said NDLEA also issued 27 official statements, participated in 36 broadcast engagements and countered dozens of misinformation items.

Mr Onumah stressed that strategic communication should be regarded as an integral component of security operations rather than an afterthought.

“Public trust is fundamental. Where credible official information is absent or unnecessarily delayed, speculation and misinformation quickly occupy the vacuum,” he said.

He urged security institutions to communicate quickly, accurately and transparently while calling on journalists to verify sensitive information and avoid reporting that could compromise operations or endanger lives.

Mr Onumah said the emerging security environment required stronger partnerships among government institutions, traditional rulers, religious leaders, journalists, civil society, businesses, academics, technology companies and communities.

He said communities remained particularly important because they often had the earliest information on suspicious movements, radicalisation, criminal recruitment and emerging tensions.

“The objective must therefore be a national security system that is preventive as well as responsive; intelligence-driven rather than merely reactive; coordinated rather than fragmented; and people-centred rather than institution-centred,” he said.

He said Nigeria’s security institutions had demonstrated significant capacity, courage and resilience, but stressed the need to improve coordination and deepen public trust continually.

Mr Onumah said security was ultimately not something the government could deliver to society from above.

“It is something institutions and citizens must build together,” he said.

items.title: How jealousy, ‘diabolical attacks’ almost derailed my music career- Salawa Abeni
items.summary: The 65-year-old began her career in 1976 with the release of her debut hit album, “Late General Murtala Ramat Mohammed.” The post How jealousy, ‘diabolical attacks’ almost derailed my music career- Salawa Abeni appeared first on Premium Times Nigeria .
items.body:
Waka music icon Salawa “Queen of Waka Music” Abeni has opened up about the challenges she faced at the beginning of her music career, revealing how jealousy and alleged “diabolical attacks” from senior colleagues nearly forced her out of the industry.

The 65-year-old began her career in 1976 with the release of her debut hit album, “Late General Murtala Ramat Mohammed.”

Speaking on “ Rubin’s Mind ” on Channels Television on Sunday night, she recounted some of the challenges she faced, including losing her voice and vomiting blood at different points in her career.

Abeni said she developed an interest in music at the age of nine and regularly performed alongside older musicians whenever they invited her to join them.

She said, “So they (the elderly ones) would sing before I got there. But when it was time for me, they would give me a stool to stand on so my mouth could reach the microphone. So when it was time for me to sing, my brother, my voice would go. I couldn’t sing. Sometimes I would even vomit blood. But what could I do? It’s a long journey. There are a lot of obstacles. You know, how do I say it in Yoruba… in English, it’s jealousy. Yes. Like, ‘You, this small girl, who is your parent?

“Where did you come from?’ Let me give examples. Let’s say you’re a musician and I’m a musician. So you would be singing before I arrived, or I would be singing before you arrived. Then people would be shouting my name, ‘The young girl, Salawa Abeni, has arrived!’ People would leave where they were to come to my side. We would be facing each other. But that is jealousy. It’s a strong thing to say people are diabolical. Well, that is it. That is exactly it.”

She further claimed that certain obstacles she faced in her career resulted from what she described as diabolical acts by some senior colleagues.

The singer said she never considered the experiences mere superstition, citing an incident in which she and her band waited backstage for another group to finish before they were allowed to perform.

“Diabolical is not superstition. Let me take you back to one experience. They would sing before I arrived, but my band was there too, so we decided to wait for each other. When they started their own performance, I sat down, and we watched. When it was my turn to sing, our amplifier back then used to connect all the microphones to bring out our voice, our tone, so that nobody could listen to me, nobody could hear me. That’s another one again.

“Another time, we went together to play. As you sat, I sat down here. When it was my turn, as you were sitting here and I was sitting here, I couldn’t sit down because I was very small; if I sat down, my mouth wouldn’t reach the microphone. So I had to stand up. Oh my God, from my own side, as we sat beside each other, very close like this, rain suddenly started falling right where I was standing, so that people who wanted to watch Salawa Abeni would run away. It is tough”, she added.

Abeni has several hit songs to her name, spanning decades of a career that has established her as one of Nigeria’s prominent waka musicians.

Some of her notable releases include “Iba Omode Iba Agba”, “Shooting Stars”, “We Are The Children”, “Maradonna”, “Cheer Up”, “Beware”, among others.

items.title: Sécurité : Un jeune entrepreneur fait don de lampes solaires au ministre de la sécurité
items.summary: Le Ministre de la Sécurité, le Camarade Mahamadou SANA, a reçu en audience, ce lundi 7 septembre 2026, un jeune entrepreneur KINDO BUSINESS SERVICES (KBS). « Je suis venu exprimer ma gratitude au Ministre pour les multiples initiatives mises en œuvre en faveur de notre sécurité », a déclaré le jeune entrepreneur à l’entame de … The post Sécurité : Un jeune entrepreneur fait don de lampes solaires
items.body:
Le Ministre de la Sécurité, le Camarade Mahamadou SANA, a reçu en audience, ce lundi 7 septembre 2026, un jeune entrepreneur KINDO BUSINESS SERVICES (KBS). « Je suis venu exprimer ma gratitude au Ministre pour les multiples initiatives mises en œuvre en faveur de notre sécurité » , a déclaré le jeune entrepreneur à l’entame de l’audience.

Au cours de cette audience, le jeune entrepreneur a expliqué qu’à l’occasion de ses voyages d’affaires, il a découvert des lampes lumineuses solaires à haute performance, particulièrement adaptées aux besoins des forces de sécurité, notamment pour les missions de surveillance, de contrôle et d’intervention dans les zones insuffisamment éclairées.

« Convaincu de leur utilité pour améliorer les conditions de travail des policiers, j’ai décidé d’en acquérir un lot au profit du ministère » , a-t-il expliqué.

Son don illustre la conviction selon laquelle chaque initiative, aussi modeste soit-elle, constitue une pierre apportée à l’édification endogène de notre Nation. Ce geste citoyen s’inscrit pleinement dans la dynamique de la Révolution Progressiste Populaire (RPP), qui appelle chaque Burkinabè à apporter sa contribution à l’effort national de construction d’un Burkina Faso souverain, résilient et prospère.

Le Camarade Ministre de la Sécurité a salué cette initiative patriotique et exprimé sa reconnaissance au donateur pour son engagement en faveur de la sécurité nationale. Il a souligné que la consolidation de la sécurité est une responsabilité partagée qui requiert l’implication de tous les fils et filles du Burkina Faso.

A un peu plus d'un an après l'exclusion de Maurice Kamto de la course à la présidentielle du 12 octobre 2025, la fédération Europe
items.body: © DR Dans une déclaration datée du 6 septembre 2026, les secrétaires départementaux MRC de la Région Europe apportent un soutien "éclairé et lucide" à leur président national élu, Maurice Kamto, au directoire et aux résolutions du Conseil national du 6 septembre 2025. A un peu plus d'un an après l'exclusion de Maurice Kamto de la course à la présidentielle du 12 octobre 2025, la fédération Europe du Mouvement pour la Renaissance du Cameroun (MRC) sort du silence. Dans un texte de deux pages signé collectivement, les responsables départementaux dénoncent ce qu'ils qualifient d'acharnement politico-judiciaire contre leur leader et contre le parti. "Notre parti dont vous tenez courageusement et avec brio le flambeau depuis la création, fait l'objet depuis toujours d'actes de déstabilisation de la part du pouvoir en place et de ses proxys", écrivent-ils à l'adresse de Maurice Kamto. L'exclusion de 2025 au cœur de la déclaration Le communiqué revient longuement sur l'invalidation de la candidature de Maurice Kamto à la présidentielle de 2025, officialisée le 5 août 2025 par le Conseil constitutionnel après un rejet initial par ELECAM pour "pluralité d'investitures" au sein du MANIDEM. Pour les signataires, cette décision est le fruit "d'un acte de cybercriminalité du MINAT" et d'un "complot d'Etat" contre le MRC. Ils citent notamment deux correspondances du ministère de l'Administration territoriale adressées à M. Thierry Okala Ebode, présenté comme un ancien militant exclu pour trahison, et au secrétaire général du parti. Une contre-attaque contre le RDPC Le texte opère un renversement d'accusation. Les secrétaires Europe rappellent que depuis juillet 2025, un militant du RDPC a officiellement saisi le MINAT, Paul Atanga Nji, de l'illégalité de toutes les instances dirigeantes de son propre parti, dont le dernier Congrès remonte à septembre 2011. Une saisine portée ensuite devant le Tribunal de grande instance du Mfoundi pour faire juger "nulles et de nul effet" les résolutions du Bureau politique du 3 novembre 2016. "Curieusement, ni le MINAT, militant du RDPC, ni le président du tribunal [...] n'a jugé utile de donner suite à sa saisine", souligne la déclaration. Et d'interroger : "Pourquoi donc tant d'agitation du RDPC et de ses prolongements étatiques contre le MRC et son Président National Elu, que vous êtes, alors que, sans avoir, enfin, organisé son Congrès [...] toutes les candidatures du RDPC vont logiquement être rejetées ?" Cap sur les législatives et municipales Au-delà de la dénonciation, le message est un appel à la mobilisation. Les responsables Europe disent faire "totalement confiance à l'intelligence des membres du directoire’’ et à leur président ‘’pour déjouer la nouvelle forfaiture du pouvoir en cours". Ils invitent Maurice Kamto et le directoire à "rester concentrés sur l'essentiel, la préparation victorieuse des élections législatives et municipales à venir" et appellent "tous les dynamiques et courageux militants à persister, avec vous et contre vents et marées". Une déclaration qui se conclut sur une profession de foi en "la vision humaniste, moderniste, développée, fondée sur le mérite, la solidarité, l'état de droit, la justice du MRC", portée selon eux par un leader "aimé par les Camerounais’’. Cet article MRC : la diaspora Europe réaffirme son soutien sans faille à Maurice Kamto est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: Sierra Leone ex-president Koroma returns after treason case dropped
items.summary: Former Sierra Leone president Ernest Bai Koroma returned to his home country Sunday, where authorities welcomed him after treason charges against him over an alleged coup attempt were dropped
items.body:
Former Sierra Leone president Ernest Bai Koroma returned to his home country Sunday, where authorities welcomed him after treason charges against him over an alleged coup attempt were dropped.

Koroma had left for Nigeria in 2024, days after being charged with treason and other offences over a deadly 2023 army uprising.

The ex-president, who led Sierra Leone from 2007 to 2018, arrived at the international airport in the capital, Freetown, accompanied by Nigerian ex-president Olusegun Obasanjo and Nigerian Foreign Minister Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu, an AFP journalist said.

He was welcomed by Sierra Leone's Foreign Minister Mohamed Rahman Swarray and officials from Koroma's party, the opposition All People's Congress (APC).

"Today I have come back home and I'm happy," Koroma told journalists, smiling.

Koroma had been cleared by Sierra Leonean authorities to travel to Nigeria for three months for medical treatment, but ended up staying more than two years.

In July, Sierra Leone's justice ministry said it had dropped the charges against him, without giving a reason.

On Friday, Vice President Mohamed Jukdeh Jalloh told a gathering of local leaders and residents in Koroma's stronghold, the central city of Makeni, that the ex-leader was returning home.

His homecoming comes ahead of presidential elections set for 2028.

The case against Koroma dated to November 2023, when armed attackers stormed a military armoury, two barracks, two prisons and two police stations, clashing with security forces.

Twenty-one people were killed in what authorities deemed a coup attempt.

Two dozen soldiers and Koroma's former bodyguard were sentenced to prison terms ranging from 50 to 100 years by a military court for their alleged roles in the mutiny.

Koroma had briefly visited Sierra Leone in July, after the charges were dropped, during a summit of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) at the invitation of current President Julius Maada Bio.

items.title: Human rights chief Türk renews call for end to Sudan war
items.summary: United Nations human rights chief Volker Türk on Monday renewed calls for an immediate ceasefire The post Human rights chief Türk renews call for end to Sudan war appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .
items.body: United Nations human rights chief Volker Türk on Monday renewed calls for an immediate ceasefire in Sudan, warning that civilians remained at imminent risk as fighting between the army and paramilitary forces intensified in several regions. The war between Sudan’s Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), which began in April 2023, has triggered one of the world’s largest humanitarian crises. More than 6 million people have been displaced within Sudan and about 4.5 million have fled to neighbouring countries, according to the United Nations. Addressing the U.N. Human Rights Council in Geneva, Türk called for an end to attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure, including markets, hospitals and fuel stations. “There needs to be an immediate ceasefire, an end to foreign involvement, and a return to inclusive civilian rule,” Türk said. He warns that the situation is deteriorating in Kordofan, Blue Nile and North and West Darfur, where civilians face what he described as an “imminent” risk. Türk’s comments came as an independent U.N.-mandated fact-finding mission presented a report on human rights violations in the conflict. Protecting human rights means holding a mirror up to those in power, challenging the status quo, and pushing the boundaries. My update to the Human Rights Council: https://t.co/vWxeXKiDH8 pic.twitter.com/anirIkKhDM — Volker Türk (@volker_turk) September 7, 2026 Drone attacks The mission said both the SAF and RSF are increasingly using long-range drones, allowing attacks to reach areas far beyond traditional front lines. Mohamed Othman, chair of the U.N. Human Rights Council’s Fact-Finding Mission for Sudan, said drone strikes had killed and injured civilians in homes, schools, hospitals, markets and displacement sites, as well as during weddings, funerals and other gatherings. The mission also alleged significant support for the RSF from individuals and entities in the United Arab Emirates, Chad, southeastern Libya and Puntland in Somalia. The UAE has repeatedly denied allegations that it provides military support to the RSF. Othman said repeated RSF drone attacks on El Obeid, the capital of North Kordofan, had affected water supplies, energy and other essential civilian infrastructure. The city is under partial siege by the RSF. The report said the SAF and RSF had both carried out attacks that harmed civilians. It cited successive RSF drone strikes on a kindergarten and hospital in Kalogie, South Kordofan, that killed 114 people, including 60 children. It also said SAF attacks on Ad-Da’ein Teaching Hospital killed at least 70 people. “Based on the evidence gathered, we found reasonable grounds to believe that both the SAF and the RSF committed serious violations of human rights and international humanitarian law which may amount to war crimes,” Othman told the council. Hospitals devastated The World Health Organization said separately on Monday that three major hospitals in Sudan’s capital, Khartoum Teaching Hospital, the Ophthalmology Hospital and the Dental Hospital, had suffered extensive damage during the conflict. Before the war, the facilities served as major referral and teaching hospitals, the WHO said. “Operating theatres have been destroyed, imaging equipment lost and several wards have collapsed,” said Abdinasir Abubakar, the WHO representative in Sudan. “Entire blocks and departments are out of service. The buildings need urgent structural repair before patients can be admitted safely.” Despite the damage, medical staff continue to treat patients in parts of the hospitals that remain usable, Abubakar said, calling for assistance to repair the facilities. The conflict has devastated Sudan’s health system, with attacks on medical facilities, shortages of medicines and supplies, and the displacement of health workers further limiting access to care. The SAF and RSF have both been accused of widespread violations against civilians during the war, including attacks on civilian areas and critical infrastructure. Both sides deny targeting civilians. The post Human rights chief Türk renews call for end to Sudan war appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

items.title: Bentiu IDP camp court opens to strengthen access to justice
items.summary: BENTIU — A new court has opened at the Bentiu internally displaced persons’ camp in South Sudan’s Unity State as authorities seek to improve access to justice for displaced communities, according to the United Nations. The Bentiu IDP Camp Court supported by the United Nations Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS), the Unity State government, the […] The post Bentiu IDP camp court opens to strengthen acc
items.body:
BENTIU — A new court has opened at the Bentiu internally displaced persons’ camp in South Sudan’s Unity State as authorities seek to improve access to justice for displaced communities, according to the United Nations.

The Bentiu IDP Camp Court supported by the United Nations Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS), the Unity State government, the Judiciary of South Sudan, and the Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs will operate from Sept. 7 to 26.

The court is expected to hear cases involving sexual and gender-based violence, drug-related offenses, and gang violence.

The Bentiu IDP Camp Court is an initiative of the Unity State Government’s Task Force on Combating Drug Abuse and Gang Violence, bringing together security, justice, and health actors.

The Court is being deployed in cooperation with the Community High Committee (CHC) of the Bentiu IDP Camp in response to repeated concerns and requests from the community for stronger justice and rule of law mechanisms to address drug use, gang violence, and sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV), particularly affecting children and youth.

Its deployment aims to bring the formal justice system directly to residents of the IDP camp and provide an opportunity for serious offences to be investigated and adjudicated.

This deployment builds on the re-establishment of the Judiciary in Unity State in May 2026 after 13 years of absence and the seven mobile courts deployed across Unity State since 2024 to combat impunity, reduce violence, deter crime and contribute to peace and security in the State.

Bentiu IDP camp is South Sudan’s largest camp for internally displaced persons, hosting more than 100,000 people.

Established as a Protection of Civilians site following the outbreak of conflict in 2013, it was redesignated as an IDP camp in 2021 and remains a major focus of UNMISS’ civilian protection efforts in Bentiu.

Following the outbreak of conflict in 2013, permanent judicial and prosecutorial capacity was restored in Bentiu only in May 2026.

To support access to justice, combat impunity, and promote accountability in support of peace and security, UNMISS has supported the deployment of seven mobile courts across Unity State since 2024, including in Southern Unity and Mayom.

These courts have resulted in the adjudication of 517 cases, following a period in which no cases were adjudicated through the formal justice system in Unity State in 2023.

Sudans Post is an independent, young, and grass roots news media organization aimed at providing readers with an alternate depiction of events that occur on Sudan, South Sudan and East Africa, and to establish an engaging social platform for readers to discover and discuss the various issues that impact the two countries and the region.

items.title: Machar trial adjourned after judge falls ill
items.summary: The trial of suspended South Sudan First Vice President Riek Machar and seven co-defendants was The post Machar trial adjourned after judge falls ill appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .
items.body: The trial of suspended South Sudan First Vice President Riek Machar and seven co-defendants was adjourned on Monday after one of the three judges fell ill, leaving the panel without the quorum needed to continue proceedings. Presiding Judge James Alala Deng said the court could not proceed because Judge Stephen Simon was unwell and unable to attend. Justice Isaac Pur Majok was also present when the trial resumed on Monday. The court had been on a week-long adjournment to consider two applications, one from the defence and another from prosecutors. The defence has asked the court to clarify and apply what it says is the correct statutory procedure for the remaining defendants. Prosecutors have filed a counter-application seeking to have the defendants questioned on the prosecution’s evidence before they are allowed to submit written defence statements. The court adjourned the proceedings until Friday, Sept. 11 to allow the prosecution to respond to the defence submissions. Machar and the seven other defendants are being tried over violence in Nasir, Upper Nile state, in March 2025, when government forces suffered heavy casualties. They face charges including treason, murder, conspiracy, terrorism, destruction of public property and crimes against humanity. Prosecutors allege that forces aligned with Machar’s Sudan People’s Liberation Army in Opposition (SPLA-IO), together with the White Army militia, killed 257 soldiers of the South Sudan People’s Defence Forces (SSPDF), including military commander General David Majur Dak, during an attack on a military garrison in Nasir. The prosecution has also alleged that military equipment worth about $58 million was destroyed or seized during the fighting. Machar and the other defendants have denied the charges.
